intro.caption: 12 December. Iceland, a valley under the fells.
Six elves went missing from the Reykjavík depot on the 11th. The snow tracks lead here.

intro.text: Nick? Can you hear me? I'm at the vault. There are Red Caps here, a lot of them, and they've got the List cabinet open...
Shout louder, little red man. The whole valley's awake now. Well. Most of it.
Your elves are in my pot. Not in the soup yet. I'm waiting for them to plump up.

choice.text: Grýla! You haven't changed a bit. Still hungry?

then.text: Always. Twelve hundred years and I've never once been full.
Or what? You'll leave me coal? I eat coal.

choice.text: Who sold you on elf stew, Grýla? It's very stringy.

then.text: A man with gold on his hair. He said the cat can eat anyone it likes.

intro.text: The gold-man said the cat can eat anyone it likes. Except the ones in red caps.
Kisa! Watch the valley, my lovely. And my boys will watch it too.

intro.caption: The Yule Cat pads down off the cliff. Below, thirteen pairs of eyes open in the dark.

intro_help.text: Thirteen Yule Lads and a cat the size of a pony. Right. Ctrl to creep, keep to the shadows, and nobody gets a good look at me.

lad_spot.text: Easy... he's squinting this way. Out of his sight, quick, or he'll yell for the cat.

cat_spot.text: The Cat's looking right at me. Don't move. Don't even jingle.

cat_near.text: There she is. If she hears me running, I'm dinner. Creep, Nick. Creep.

first_treasure.text: {thing}. That's the {lad}'s! Grýla must have taken it off him. If he sees me with it, I'll bet he comes straight over for it.

returned_1.text: My... my {thing}! Mother said it was gone for good.

returned_2.text: {thing}! The red man brought it back. She never gives anything back.

returned_2.caption: Two Lads, whispering behind a turf wall: 'Why are we guarding her pot, anyway?'

mutiny.text: Three of us! He gave back three!
Mother takes our things. The Cat bites our ankles. And the gold-man brought her a pot big enough for SIX.
Every year, children leave us shoes in the window. This one leaves us our own spoons back!
We're not watching for her any more. The sheep gate's open, red man. Take the old track up the west side. Nobody looks there.

mutiny.caption: The Yule Lads are on your side now.

barracks.text: Red Caps. Asleep, all six of them. 'Except the ones in red caps'... Grýla, you've just told me how to get my elves home.

cap_wont_fit.text: Got one. Too small for me, but it'll fit an elf a treat. One for each of them, if I can manage it.

caps_all.text: Six caps, six elves. Now for the cave.

redcap_stir.text: Wha—! Who's there? ...Mmf. Dreaming about chimneys again.

cave_enter.text: That's her, snoring. And that's my elves, in a cage, next to a pot. Of course it is.
Once I open that cage, it'll be a dash for the sleigh with the Cat behind us. Best be ready.

headshot.caption: A signed photograph in a gilt frame: a man with very golden hair, giving a thumbs-up.
'To Grýla — a fantastic ogre. The best.'

free.text: SANTA! You came! She was going to put us in with the turnips!
Shh! Not a peep. Quick now, put these on.

free_no_caps.text: Put what on? You haven't got anything, Santa.
...Then we run. Fast. Stay right behind me.

free_few_caps.text: {caps} red caps for six of us? Ooh, tight. The rest of us will just have to be quick.

free_caps.text: Red caps! The Cat won't touch the ones in red caps, everybody knows that. Cap on, everyone!

chase.text: Elves, stay on my heels! To the sleigh, RUN!

cat_leaps.text: She's off the cliff! She's coming!

cat_stunned.text: Right on the nose! Keep going!

capped_pass.text: She sniffed right past me! The caps WORK!

outro.caption: Blitzen shakes his harness. Sleigh bells ring out across the valley, and the Yule Cat bolts.

outro.text: Bells. She never could stand them. In you get, all {kept} of you.
Red man! This way, round the back of the fish racks. Mother's coming down the cliff.

outro.caption: The Yule Lads lead the sleigh out under the fells. Grýla's bellowing fades behind the hills.

outro.text: Holly? Holly, come in. We've got them.
